title: The Peak-End Rule in UX Design
summary: This lesson explains the Peak-End Rule, a psychological principle where users judge an experience based on its most intense point and its end. By designing intentional peaks and polishing the final interaction, designers can significantly improve user memory and satisfaction.

transcript.text: Same UX, different memory. Here is why.
It only remembers the peak moment and the end.
Two-second flow or two-day vacation, same wiring.
But one ends with a confetti animation.
Same time spent, but the first one rates 40% higher in memory.
The aha moment when filters click, the shipping date that beats expectation.
One delight beats five neutral interactions.
But the rule cuts both ways.
A perfect onboarding that ends with a payment error?
Forget the average. Polish the end.

on_screen_text: Forget the average. Polish the end.
before_after: A standard checkout success screen (Cold Ending) is compared to one with a confetti animation (Joyful Ending), showing a 40% increase in memory recall.
